messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Paging on-call: elevated streaming latency in `inference-serving` (us-west1). p95/p99 breach > service SLO. please acknowledge.

kai: ack. looking now. p95 ~520ms, p99 ~3.2s for streaming endpoints. seeing big tail between 14:10-14:25 UTC. root: 2387654321

sara: i'm on infra. which nodes are hot? any ECC/thermal alerts?

kai: grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123/latency?orgId=1 — streaming tail spike at 14:10. seems localized to us-west1-a.

alex: pulling node metrics. `kubectl get pods -o wide -n prod | grep streamer` shows many streamer pods on gpu-node-5a3f and gpu-node-7d2c.

maria: quick check of gpu health: `ssh gpu-node-5a3f` then `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i ecc -A3` returns repeated 'Correctable ECC errors' increments and gpu_temp ~86C with throttle events.

kai: runtime logs show streaming stalls with kv cache misses + kernel retries. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z INF stream_chunk id=xyz delay=1200ms kv_miss=true
2026-03-15T14:12:04Z WARN gpu=5a3f ecc_correctable=42 thermal_throttle=true
```

sara: that lines up. likely flaky gpu node hitting thermal throttle + accumulative ECC correctables => kernel stalls => scheduler backpressure => tail latency surge.

kai: customer impact: ~8% of us-west1 streaming requests >2s in window. CS notified for impacted top-tier customers.

maria: mitigation plan: cordon + drain `gpu-node-5a3f`, evict streamer pods to other gpu nodes, and enable overflow to `cpu-fallback-pool`. also spin up spare nodes in dedicated pool.

alex: commands ready:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-5a3f
kubectl drain gpu-node-5a3f --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force\```

kai: cordoning now. routing new sessions away. ✅

incident-bot: action logged: `kai` cordoned `gpu-node-5a3f` at 2026-03-15T14:16:12Z.

sara: requesting hardware ops for replacement. tagging @hw-ops.

hw-ops: acknowledged. rack-level access ETA ~45m. we can temp isolate the card and run stress tests + memcheck.

maria: after cordon+drain p95 dropped to ~150ms within 2m, p99 down to ~600ms; occasional 1.2–1.8s tails as evacuations finish.

kai: enabling routing fallback for streaming to `rxx-small` (CPU-backed) for new sessions above threshold to reduce tail latency. applying rollout now.

alex: autoscaler triggered: POST /internal/autoscale?pool=dedicated-us-west1&count=2 to add capacity.

sara: collect traces for postmortem: annotate KV cache flushes, kernel retries, save `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi` snapshots from the node before handing to hw-ops.

kai: posted status update: "We are experiencing elevated streaming latencies in US-West; mitigation in progress. No data loss; degraded performance for some customers." CS echoing to affected customers.

maria: hardware logs excerpt:
```
Device 0000:3b:00.0 ECC errors: correctable 124 -> 167 (delta 43)
Thermal throttle events: 6
Power cap adjusted by driver
```

sara: next steps: hw-ops to test/replace card, infra to reimage node and run soak for 30m before rejoining. created INC-2026-2387.

kai: handing off on-call to tim for overnight monitoring. tim — i'll dm you the runbook and pointer to the short-lived fallback flags.

tim: taking over. ping me if spikes reappear. set alert to page at 5% latency breach in 10m window.

incident-bot: incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. last_message_ts: 2387654399

sara: retrospective checklist: verify gpu cooling configs, node thermal thresholds, add early ECC-correctable-rate alert (+10/min) and consider auto-migrate when ECC > N for 5m.

maria: noted. opening infra-ticket and adding item to weekly oncall sync.

kai: closing channel for now. will attach logs to INC-2026-2387 and draft postmortem tomorrow. 🙏
